title: Training in Molecular Virology and Viral Pathogenesis
text:
The major goal of the University of Iowa Virology Predoctoral Training Program is to produce
outstanding independent virologists who will pursue careers in academic or other virology-
related careers. Students in the program will spend 90% of their time pursuing virology
research under the supervision of a funded participating faculty member. Laboratory work will
be supplemented by opportunities to hone their skills in data presentation and teaching.

title: Defining multifunctional roles for proteins in development and disease
text:
Understanding the multifunctional roles of proteins is essential for designing therapeutic strategies to treat
genetic causes of disease, yet our knowledge of these secondary roles for many proteins remains incomplete.
We will elucidate the multifunctional roles of a protein involved in cancer, microcephaly, and infertility, while also
using our expertise in high resolution 3D X-Ray imaging and artificial intelligence to establish an experimental
workflow that will accelerate the discovery of multifunctional protein roles in model organisms such as Drosophila
melanogaster and Xenopus laevis.

title: Validated Immunoassays to Accelerate Therapeutic Genome Editing INDs
text:
The overarching goal is to optimize immunoassays focused on addressing the safety and efficiency of somatic
cell genome editing in human clinical trials. These studies will provide validated methods and reliable tools for
accurately assessing in vivo events and best practices to meet regulatory requirements focused on genome
editing therapeutics.

title: Cancer Cell Biology Research Program
text:

PROJECT NARRATIVE

title: Extending the longevity of implantable biomedical devices by therapeutic regulation of the foreign body response
text:
Implanted biomaterials can induce an inflammatory reaction at the tissue-biomaterial interface characterized by
foreign body response (FBR) and implant failure. We will examine the CD13-dependent mechanisms and
molecules that regulate FBGC fusion and FBR in response to biomaterials to prevent FBR related pathology.

title: Hepatocytes and skeletal myocytes shape immunity to mRNA-LNP encoded protein
text:
Non-immune cells that take up mRNA delivered by lipid nanoparticle include hepatocytes and skeletal
myocytes. Although there is an urgent need to better understand the mechanisms driving immunity to mRNA-
encoded proteins, there is limited data describing how these specific cell types modulate the antigen-specific
adaptive immune response. The objective of this proposal is to comprehensively interrogate the mechanisms
by which these cell types modulate immunity and to leverage microRNA-mediated regulation of mRNA
expression to enhance immunity induced by an established tumor-associated antigen and pathogen vaccine
strategies.

title: Metabolic Reprogramming of the Alveolar Stem Cell Niche in Pulmonary Fibrosis
text:
Pulmonary fibrosis is linked to a failure of regeneration that involves epithelial-fibroblast interactions. This
project will study the role of a metabolic enzyme, nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), that reprograms
cellular function and behavior of fibroblasts from a pro-regenerative to a pro-fibrotic phenotype.

title: A comprehensive thermodynamic and structural characterization of ion channel function and its regulation by the lipid bilayer composition
text:
Because K+ selective ion channels are essential regulators of cell excitability, their dysfunction underlies a myriad
of human pathological conditions that make them excellent targets for drugs to treat very diverse diseases, such
as: LQT syndrome, arrhythmia, epilepsy, autoimmune diseases and diabetes. It follows that understanding the
function-structure correlations of K+ channels at atomic resolution will pave the road to develop highly-specific
therapeutic drugs to correct channelopathies. The central tenet of this grant application is how the structure
determine the function of ion channel and how this relationship is influenced by the cell membrane lipid
composition.

title: Development of a universal approach to block inhibitors for protein replacement therapy
text:
Inhibitors against biological drugs are the major factor to lead to therapeutic failure in patients with rare genetic
disorders after protein replacement treatment. The current approaches to overcome inhibitors are either
expensive or not effective in all patients. This Phase I project will explore a universal strategy to block biologics
inhibitors for repeated administration using the engineered protein-M derived from mycoplasma.

title: A precision therapy approach to red cell transfusion for sickle cell disease
text:
The overall theme of this proposal is to develop a precision medicine approach to red blood cell matching for
patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). We present innovative solutions to major clinical challenges of Rh
alloimmunization in SCD. We aim to determine the effectiveness of RH genotype matched donor units on Rh
alloimmunization, develop a low-cost RH sequencing assay with integrated interpretation to facilitate widespread
implementation of RH genotype matching, and generate customized pluripotent stem cell-derived red blood cells
with variant Rh for precise antibody identification, with the ultimate goal of improving transfusion outcomes.

title: Dissecting the role and mechanism of EML4-ALK condensates in oncogenic signaling and tumor growth
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE. Precision medicines that specifically target proteins that drive cancer growth are
leading to improved responses in many advanced-stage cancer patients. This molecular treatment approach
requires a firm understanding of the biological mechanism of cancer development and progression. The studies
in this grant proposal focus on the characterization of a new mechanism of oncogenic signaling, focusing on the
role of biomolecular condensates in ALK-driven lung cancer, with the overall goal of laying a foundation for
developing a new suite of molecular treatments in the future that better control this cancer through improved
precision medicine strategies.

title: CardioExcyte 96: High-Throughput, Non-Invasive Platform for Cardiac Electrophysiology and Toxicology
text:
The CardioExcyte 96 system will help improve our understanding of heart diseases and the effects of
medications on heart health. By enabling researchers to more accurately study heart function and the potential
risks of drugs, this technology could lead to safer medications and better treatments for heart-related conditions,
ultimately benefiting public health by reducing the risk of drug-induced heart problems, improving cardiovascular
care and discovering new therapeutic targets.

title: Computational and functional screens to identify actionable neuroblastoma drivers
text:
New molecular biology and molecular genetic tools in the genomics era were anticipated to transform therapy
for children with hard-to-cure forms of cancer, such as neuroblastoma. That promise has not been realized for
individuals with cancer that does not harbor highly recurrent, targetable mutations, as is the case for children
with neuroblastoma. Our project tests the idea that a new, deep learning algorithm integrating gene expression,
copy-number alterations, and survival outcome can inform high throughput screening assays and reveal new,
targetable oncogenic drivers and new biologically-grounded biomarkers for risk stratification and treatment –
finally realizing the potential of the current, multi-omics revolution to improve outcomes for children with
neuroblastoma.

title: Core 3 Biostatistics
text: Core 3 – Summary The Biostatistics Core (Core 3) provides comprehensive statistical and bioinformatics support for all components of the SPORE in Leukemia, with the goal of ensuring rigorous, reproducible, and collaborative analytical support across laboratory, translational, and clinical research domains. The Core works closely with investigators participating in Research Projects, the Developmental Research Program, the Career Enhancement Program, and other SPORE Cores to offer customized biostatistical services tailored to specific study needs. Core 3 is co- directed by Rafael Irizarry, PhD, and Svitlana Tyekucheva, PhD, both leading experts in biostatistics and computational biology. Dr. Irizarry is Professor in the DFCI Department of Data Science and the Department of Biostatistics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, where he also serves as Chair of Data Science. A pioneer in statistical genomics, his research focuses on high-dimensional data analysis including single-cell sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and epigenetics. He is a founder of the Bioconductor Project and developer of widely used open-source tools and educational resources. Dr. Irizarry will oversee genomic and bioinformatics activities of the Core and guide integration of statistical methodologies across projects. Dr. Tyekucheva is a Principal Research Scientist and independent investigator in the DFCI Department of Data Science and Harvard Biostatistics. She specializes in high-throughput sequencing, multi-omics data integration, and clinical/translational study analysis. As current director of the Biostatistics Core for the DF/HCC Prostate Cancer SPORE, Dr. Tyekucheva brings deep experience managing correlative and clinical data. She will lead oversight of all biostatistical and clinical data activities, supervising staff and ensuring effective support for study design, analysis, and data sharing. The Core's first aim is to deliver expert guidance in the planning, design, conduct, analysis, and reporting of studies. This includes support for laboratory-based experiments, genomic and bioinformatics analyses, animal models, translational investigations, clinical trials, and associated correlative studies. By embedding statistical collaboration at every stage, the Core enhances the scientific rigor of each project. The second aim focuses on consultation for all aspects of data management. This includes advising on the collection, integration, quality assurance, transfer, storage, and sharing of data. The Core ensures the use of reliable statistical and computational software and helps align laboratory findings with clinical parameters and outcomes through coordination with research databases. The third aim is to provide timely, short-term biostatistics and computational biology consulting to all SPORE investigators. This flexible support allows researchers to address analytical needs quickly and effectively, helping to sustain momentum across the SPORE’s diverse research activities.

title: Histone methyltransferase, Setd2, in substance use disorders
text:
This proposal investigates the role of Setd2, a chromatin modifying enzyme, in cocaine substance use
disorder. By evaluating a novel Setd2 inhibitor we aim to understand and mitigate the gene regulatory
mechanisms underlying addiction.

title: Transgenic Core (TGC)
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – TRANSGENIC The mission of the Transgenic Shared Resource (TGC) is to provide Salk Cancer Center (SCC) members access to cutting-edge technologies for creating genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs). GEMMs are critical tools that enable researchers to model human cancer, to analyze and functionally manipulate specific genes, and to test potential therapeutic interventions. Established in 1994 with CCSG and Institutional funds, the facility remains relevant to SCC researchers today. On average, the TGC serves 42% (13/31) of SCC members annually who are responsible for 74% of all TGC services based on recharges. The TGC provides services for state-of- the-art genome editing and to generate and maintain transgenic mice. These include: 1) the microinjection of DNA constructs, CRISPR/Cas9, and lentiviral vectors into early mouse embryos, 2) microinjection of gene- targeted mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells into blastocysts, 3) in-vitro fertilization , 4) embryo and sperm cryopreservation, 5) re-derivation of mouse lines provided from non-standard sources, 6) gene targeting in mouse ES cells, 7) targeting vector design and construction, 8) de novo derivation of ES cell lines, and 9) ES cell expansion and preparation for microinjection. In addition, the TGC offers services for the injection of human ES cell lines and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines into immunodeficient mice to assess their ability to form teratomas. The TGC develops new techniques and applications and provides immediate access to individuals with prior knowledge of transgenic and knock out mouse models. For those lacking experience, the TGC provides individual consultations, as well as group meetings, to discuss strategies for model development and recent innovations in transgenic and gene targeting technologies that may be relevant to the researcher’s goals. Overall, the transgenic and gene-targeting services provided by the TGC greatly increase the pace at which mouse models can be generated, and at significantly lower cost, than commercial sources. All activities of the TGC are overseen by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).

title: Contactless activation of the mechanosensory system by photoacoustic stimulation
text:
This proposal develops a platform for non-contact stimulation of mechanosensitive and thermosensitive ion
channels using pulsed light to generate localized mechanical forces via the photoacoustic effect. Building on
findings that such stimulation elicits perceptual responses in humans, we aim to adapt and validate the method
for general use in cellular and animal models. The approach is capable of spatial and temporal resolution and
does not require genetic modification and thus offers a general tool for probing mechanobiological systems.

title: Molecular Prediction of Myeloma Initiation Molecular Prediction of Myeloma Initiation
text:
The next frontier in cancer research is early detection and prevention, and my overarching goal is to apply this
to myeloma by defining the first steps of disease development and treating it early before symptoms occur. We
will redefine the risk factors of race and chronological age based on underlying biological traits. We will identify
ancestry risk scores and genomic signatures that increase the risk of developing myeloma in Black individuals
and dissect the molecular mechanisms of “effective age” of the tissue of origin (bone marrow).

title: Structural and Biochemical Studies of HIV and MMTV Retroviral Integration onto Nucleosome-bound Target DNA
text:
Catalytic integration of viral DNA into the target host genome is a hallmark of the infection
cycle of all retroviruses, including the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). Using in vitro
biochemistry and structural biology, my research aims to define how and where retroviral
intasomes, which are the molecular machines that mediate integration, catalyze viral DNA
integration into chromatin assemblies. The outcome of the work will provide novel insights into
patterns and preferences of viral DNA integration into and around nucleosomes and dissect the
structural bases of integration into chromatin.

title: Dual Functionality of Ceramide in Human Microvascular Endothelial Function
text:
Sphingolipids can promote or prevent microvascular endothelial dysfunction, which precedes large artery
atherosclerosis. We hypothesize that formation of ceramide, although detrimental following chronic exposure, is
necessary for proper microvascular function. The results of this study could greatly expand our understanding of
local tissue perfusion and provide novel targets for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
